teaser.text: Boston Scientific is a medical-device company: it sells tools and implants that help clinicians diagnose and treat disease. Its dollar begins with a provider’s purchase, then passes through manufacturing, research, selling and support costs before the remainder becomes operating income.

stock.title: Boston Scientific stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Boston Scientific's forecast weighs recovery, competition, cash generation and valuation across bear, base and bull scenarios.
stock.opening: Boston Scientific's probability-weighted price is $78.68 by October 2029, with the base case carrying 54% probability. It hinges on earnings recovery, franchise defense, Penumbra integration and cash generation after the operating disruption.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Boston Scientific's business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Boston Scientific's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to substantial upside, but with a wide range of outcomes. The probability-weighted price is $53.78 in October 2027, implying a 21% total return. It reaches $64.69 in October 2028, implying 46%. By October 2029, the weighted price is $78.68, implying 77%.

The final-date range runs from $32.63 in the bear case to $135.23 in the bull case. Today’s price is $44.39. The forecast assigns 27% to the bear case, 54% to the base case and 19% to the bull case, so the central judgment is gradual recovery rather than either collapse or rapid reacceleration.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Boston Scientific, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The drivers are outage-related sales recovery, normalized orders, cash generation, Penumbra closing and financing, physician adoption and repeat use of FARAWAVE Ultra and ICE imaging—ultrasound pictures made from inside the heart. On October 28, 2026, the new outlook must clarify recovery and cash generation. By year-end 2026, Penumbra’s closing and financing will test integration. In the second half of 2027, FARAWAVE Ultra and ICE imaging must translate into adoption. Through 2029, restructuring cash costs and savings will test efficiency gains.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Boston Scientific really make?

paragraphs.text: A stricter owner measure also subtracts stock-based compensation. The expense is not a current cash payment, but employees receive shares, which can dilute existing owners. Cash can fund acquisitions, debt repayment and other investment, yet it still does not prove that a new device has won clinical acceptance.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Boston Scientific today?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, tells us how much investors pay for each dollar of profit. Boston Scientific reported 2025 GAAP diluted EPS of $1.94 and adjusted EPS of $3.06. GAAP is the standardized accounting result; adjusted EPS removes selected costs such as amortization and acquisition charges. The forward P/E therefore looks lower because it assumes earnings will rise, but that comparison works only when both ratios use the same definition of profit. On the table’s figures, the implied earnings step-up is about 37%.

blocks.heading: What has Boston Scientific guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Management’s July 2026 outlook called for 5%–6% organic sales growth. It also called for $3,800 million of free cash flow for FY 2026. After the cyber disruption, management said it would provide a new outlook on October 28, 2026.

blocks.heading: Did Boston Scientific keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Adjusted operating margin was 28.0% against a 27.6% target. Mahoney’s annual bonus reached 173% of target. These results show a measurable link between pay and performance, although they do not show whether the targets were demanding enough.

blocks.heading: What do Boston Scientific’s last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: As of October 17, 2026, Boston Scientific had not reported its third-quarter results. The accounts therefore support two separate conclusions: the underlying growth engines had weakened before the cyber incident, and the incident left the amount of delayed or recoverable revenue unresolved.

blocks.heading: What should Boston Scientific watchers look for next?

paragraphs.text: On October 28, Boston Scientific plans to report third-quarter results and provide a new operating and financial outlook. Investors should look for the amount of outage-related sales management says it recovered, whether customer orders have normalized and what it now expects for full-year cash generation. Restored operations are encouraging, but they do not show how much demand was permanently lost.

Next come the Penumbra closing and the EP launches. Closing would begin the integration period and the expected initial EPS dilution. The second-half 2027 launch of FARAWAVE Ultra and the entry into ICE imaging will test the product-led recovery story. Launches alone will not prove that physicians have adopted the products.
